what_happened: The person running Athena started a verifier transfer fix by hand while a drain batch was running. The two builds together pushed free disk below the 10 GB a writer needs. The disk guard stopped one batch job with an environment message and held it. The the person running Athena stopped the batch and deleted the held job's 8.4 GB build by hand. They plan to restart the batches after the hand run finishes.
cause: Disk is not managed as a budget. Athena does not compare free disk with the combined build size of running work, a hand-run job and the folders of held jobs. Nothing makes a hand-started job and a drain share that budget. The limit is only found when the free-disk guard fires. Athena frees no space itself, so a person must clear it.
prevention: Add a disk budget that every build start must pass, whether it comes from a drain or from a hand-run command. Before starting, it takes free disk minus the writer minimum minus the estimated size of builds already running. If that is not enough, the new start waits or is refused with a message that names the other running build. When disk runs low, Athena should also reclaim build folders it can safely remove, such as the folders of held jobs. It should mark a job stopped for an environment reason as waiting, not failed, and resume it once space returns.
proposed_request: Add a disk budget check to Athena that covers every build start, including hand-run commands and drain jobs. Before a producer build starts, Athena must check that free disk, minus the 10 GB writer minimum and minus the estimated size of builds already running or held, is enough for the new build. The estimate can come from recent build sizes. If it is not enough, a drain job waits and a hand-run command is refused with a message that names the running builds. A job stopped by the free-disk guard must be recorded as waiting for the environment, not failed. It must resume automatically when space is available. Athena should also remove the build folders of held jobs that it can safely recreate, before it refuses a start. Acceptance: (1) a test with a fake disk shows a second start is refused or queued while one build is running and the combined need exceeds free disk; (2) a test shows a job stopped for low disk is not marked failed and resumes once space returns; (3) a test shows a held job's build folder is reclaimed when space is short; (4) the refusal message names the other running build.
